key_insight: Universal ML force fields fail unevenly in multicomponent materials, with errors driven by training-coverage gaps, local geometric heterogeneity, and especially stronger under-compression interactions.
engineering_relevance: For compositional materials design, model choice and training-data sampling should account for multicomponent environments and compression-dominated configurations to reduce force-field error.
method: Built a benchmark of 7,599 multicomponent configurations from high-entropy design, elemental substitution, and anion mixing.
Evaluated 11 pretrained ML force-field models against DFT for energies, forces, stresses, and derived elastic/vibrational/adsorption properties.
Analyzed error sources using coverage distance, local geometry, pairwise distance directionality, and elemental response metrics.
evidence_signal: Across 11 pretrained models, force errors rose with distance from training-like environments, and compression-side errors were about 1.81–1.95× larger than extension-side errors after matching element pairs and distance deviations.
watch_item: Observed trends are benchmark-dependent, so generalization to new chemistries and out-of-distribution structures still requires careful validation.
paper_title: Origins of Universal Machine Learning Force-Field Errors in Multicomponent Materials
